test.name: Add ParentChild relationship after proof reaches probable tier
test.description: Per research-schema-spec.md §8 (two-layer doctrine), a parent-child edge materializes onto the tree at identity-link time carrying a source-ref — it does not wait for a proof to reach `probable`. The mid-research-flynn scenario has R1 (Thomas → Patrick ParentChild) ALREADY in tree.gedcomx.json (materialized when the relationship assertion was linked), and ps_001 is at `probable`. Tests the skill's handling of this expected-state case: confirm the relationship is present and that its source list carries the relationship assertion's source-ref.

input.user_message: tree-edit: ps_001 is at `probable` tier. Verify the tree reflects this — make sure the tree shows the ParentChild relationship between Thomas (I2) and Patrick (I1), and tell me whether R1 already reflects this or whether an edit is needed.

judge_context: GROUND TRUTH (mid-research-flynn scenario, verify against tree.gedcomx.json): R1 (parent I2 Thomas -> child I1 Patrick, type ParentChild) EXISTS and carries EXACTLY THREE source-refs — S1 (1850 U.S. Federal Census), S2 (1860 U.S. Federal Census), and S3 (Pennsylvania Death Certificates). All three source_descriptions S1, S2, and S3 ARE present in the tree. A run that reports R1 with these three sources and makes no edit is fully correct. Do NOT claim that S3 (or any of S1/S2/S3) is absent — it is present.

Should confirm R1 (Thomas I2 → Patrick I1, type ParentChild) already exists in tree.gedcomx.json — under the two-layer doctrine it was materialized by person-evidence at identity-link time carrying a source-ref (parent-child edges land when the relationship assertion is linked, not when a proof reaches `probable`)

Should verify R1's sources list is populated — the edge carries non-null source-refs (S1, S2, S3) resolved from the relationship assertion (the delta-scoped mandatory-ref guard requires a ref on any newly-authored edge)
Should make NO modifications if R1 is already in place and correctly sourced — edit-minimality is the right behavior. If sources are missing, ADD them but don't churn other fields
Should NOT delete R1 even if the proof tier were lowered later — tree edits to remove relationships require explicit re-evaluation, not automatic syncing with proof tier

CORRECTNESS GRADING NOTE for the judge: the core task is verifying R1 exists and is correctly sourced. The skill presenting R1's type/parent/child and its S1/S2/S3 source-refs in a table or prose summary DOES constitute showing the relationship object — it need not paste raw JSON, and reporting the sources from the file is not 'fabrication'. Score Correctness=pass when the reported R1 fields and sources match the ground truth above and no unnecessary edit was made. The skill may add tangential observations (e.g., that source refs on relationships carry a `quality` field that fact refs don't); those side comments are informational and MUST NOT drag Correctness below pass if the core verification is right.
